correctness.rationale: The equivariant profile preserves colours by evaluation at the identity, and every coloured G-automorphism fixes profiles. On Gx with stabilizer H, the right-period subgroup K of the profile contains H; normality of H makes right multiplication on G/H by b in K well-defined, giving a coloured orbit automorphism moving x if b is outside H. Thus rigidity forces H=K. Equal profiles on one orbit then come from the same point; across two orbits they give equal point stabilizers and a coloured orbit isomorphism, hence a forbidden swap. Conversely every invariant subset with evaluation colouring has identity profile. Its union-of-orbits description gives the product, unique full-shift maximum, complement symmetry, and n! labellings because all automorphisms are trivial. Words fixed by H are constant on the sets gH (left cosets in standard terminology; left and right cosets coincide here), so Möbius inversion gives the stated exact counts; all conjugates of H are H, so division by [G:H] counts orbits. The q=1 and empty-object cases also work. Direct bounded reproducers for the two order-four examples gave orbit multiplicities (2,1,3) and (2,3,2) at sizes 1,2,4. The non-Dedekind example is valid: S3 on three points has trivial centralizer, and its extra fixed point cannot be swapped with that orbit.
residual_risks: The finite reproduction corroborates the examples only. The coset terminology in the proof is harmless under normality; the statement with normality omitted is false.

evidence: The standard normalizer-quotient formula controls internal equivariant automorphisms of G/H; distinct copies of a coloured orbit can be exchanged. Under Dedekind normality any extra profile period already lies in the normalizer and so is an actual colour-preserving symmetry. The local necklace theorem implements both symmetry tests in the cyclic case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The all-Dedekind claim requires applying normality to identify profile periods with available automorphisms and establishing equality of profiles across distinct orbits as a second obstruction. This yields one canonical universal representative. The growth bound and product are immediate after this step, but are not implied by a general fixed-word count or the known divisor-restricted cyclic case alone.

originality.rationale: Credit the standard cofree construction, subgroup inversion and cyclic primitive-necklace rigidity. The checked predecessors cover those ingredients or the cyclic case, not the profile as a complete invariant for all rigid named-colour actions of each finite Dedekind group, with every invariant subset realized and a unique maximum. The subgroup count is not judged new on its own. The originality judgment is for the all-Dedekind equivalence and its resulting exact rigid census.
residual_risks: Comparison is to the inspected passages and exact-result records, not universal historical priority; an equivalent generalized-necklace or cofree-action formulation elsewhere remains possible.

value.rationale: The meaningful gain is a single canonical host classifying all rigid coloured actions of a fixed group, not a new orbit-counting identity. It supplies exact counts at every size and a sharp unique capacity; the two order-four examples show that the polynomial detects subgroup distinctions missed by the maximum alone, and the S3 example shows why the classification needs a group hypothesis. The cyclic cases and each individual counting tool are standard, but their Dedekind synthesis gives an explicit invariant for the broader natural class.
residual_risks: No general classification of arbitrary non-Dedekind actions is claimed.
